seo.shortDescription: What the EU, Canada, Mexico, China, Japan and Korea charge on U.S. medical devices, lab instruments and measuring equipment, by market and product, with each market's device-approval rules.
keywords: China tariff on US medical devices
EU tariff on US medical devices

intro: Tariffs are a small obstacle for this chapter: Canada, Mexico, South Korea, Singapore and (since July 1, 2026) the EU charge nothing on U.S. instruments, and Japan, Taiwan and the UK charge low MFN rates. China is the exception, adding a flat 10% on top of its own rates. What decides whether a U.S. device can be sold is regulatory approval — a CE mark under the EU's Medical Device Regulation, a Health Canada licence, NMPA registration in China, PMDA approval in Japan — and, for lasers, thermal-imaging, navigation and some inspection equipment, U.S. export controls (see Export rules). Each market's regulator is listed below.

profile.headline: The EU is the largest market ($30.81B, 29% of the chapter), and the Netherlands alone buys $12.12B — the largest single buyer — followed by Germany ($6.51B). Most medical instruments already entered at 0–4.2%; the 2026 framework removes the rest. The real gate is the Medical Device Regulation: a CE mark, and an EU authorised representative for a non-EU manufacturer.

assumptions: MFN rates are the World Bank/UNCTAD WITS (TRAINS) simple-average applied rates for one representative six-digit subheading per heading — the subheading with the largest 2025 U.S. exports in that heading (for example 9018.90 for medical instruments) — for the most recent year WITS holds (2019–2023). National 8–10-digit lines can differ, and many medical devices carry lower rates than the sample.
USMCA (Mexico, Canada), KORUS (South Korea) and the U.S.–Singapore FTA apply 0% to qualifying U.S.-origin goods; the normal-rate column shows each market's MFN rate for goods that do not qualify.
For the EU, Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 zeroes out Chapter 90 from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029; the normal-rate column shows the rate the EU charged before then.

China's cells add the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods to its MFN rate. China's 2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods, valid unless a line is covered by an exclusion until December 31, 2026, are not added because exclusions are granted line by line. The 43 medical-device lines on China's Board of Trade list have no published tariff cut yet.
Taiwan shows its MFN rates: the U.S.–Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade (signed February 2026) has not entered into force. UK and Japan show MFN rates.
